rules: The Title Descriptor dataset gives the estate interest and class of title for each registered estate and interest in England and Wales.
A title number can have only one class of title.
Every registered title has a title number, estate and class of title.
An application awaiting registration has an associated title number but no estate or class-of-title information.
The dataset also represents registration applications that HM Land Registry has started but not completed.
Title Descriptor, National Polygon and UPRN data are separated to make the datasets smaller and easier to manage and maintain.
The title number is the unique identifier used to link Title Descriptor data to other HM Land Registry products.
Title number is a mandatory character field identifying a registered title.
Estate Interest is an optional character field.
Class of Title is an optional character field.
Registered Status is a mandatory character field.
A Registered Status value of Pending means the application is being processed.
A blank Registered Status field means that the title is registered.
Change Indicator is a mandatory character field.
Change Indicator values are New, Changed and Deleted.
HM Land Registry records three classes of title for freehold land.
HM Land Registry records four classes of title for leasehold land.
Absolute title is the best class of title.
A qualified title may be granted for a specific defect, which is specified in the register.
start_date_match accepts match, before, since or an empty value.
end_date_match accepts match, before, since or an empty value.
entry_date_match accepts match, before, since or an empty value.
The geometry filter accepts one or more WKT geometry strings.
geometry_entity accepts entity identifiers whose geometries are used for spatial filtering.
geometry_reference accepts references whose entity geometries are used for spatial filtering.
geometry_curie accepts CURIE values whose matching entity geometries are used for spatial filtering.
within is an allowed geometry_relation value.
equals is an allowed geometry_relation value.
disjoint is an allowed geometry_relation value.
intersects is an allowed geometry_relation value.
touches is an allowed geometry_relation value.
contains is an allowed geometry_relation value.
covers is an allowed geometry_relation value.
coveredby is an allowed geometry_relation value.
overlaps is an allowed geometry_relation value.
crosses is an allowed geometry_relation value.
The 1m composite DSM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The 1m DSM is produced from the last or only laser return.
The DSM includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as the terrain surface.
The 2022 product combines Time Stamped archive surveys with National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where surveys repeat, the newest best-resolution source is used.
Bilinear interpolation is used before merging when source data is resampled.
The 2022 composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000 through 2 April 2022.
Esri Image Services were replaced by equivalent WCS and WMS services under the open-standards policy.
WMS provides a summarised elevation view while WCS provides elevation values.
WCS GeoTIFF responses use -3.4028235e+38 as the NoData value.
Grid heights are calculated at pixel centres, so adjacent tiles do not overlap and do not share common edge values.
Mean high and low water lines are assigned constant heights based on an average for each tile derived from local tide tables.
The per-tile tidal averaging can create a small discrete height step between adjacent tiles.
For permanent tidal water, mean-low-water height is extended to the tile edge to complete the grid tile.
Foreshore heights are interpolated between mean-high-water and mean-low-water heights.
Contour products contain no contours between the mean-high-water and mean-low-water lines.
The shapefile representation abbreviates the GML propertyValue attribute to PROP_VALUE because of the 10-character field-name limit.
Spot heights are selected algorithmically from the highest source-data point within each enclosed contour.
Interpolated spot heights are not guaranteed to be summits or the highest real-world point of a feature.
All current OS Terrain 50 spot-height features are attributed as generic.
